Based on the logs from docindex-3 and the pod status, I now have a clear understanding of the problem. The issue is that the StatefulSet's pods are configured with a CLUSTER_SIZE environment variable set to 3 (the original replica count), but the scaling operation only updated the StatefulSet replica count to 5. The new pods (docindex-3 and docindex-4) are failing readiness checks because they see themselves as outside the configured cluster size.

Let me update the ticket with the resolution.

input.note:
**Cause:** The docindex StatefulSet was scaled from 3 to 5 replicas, but the CLUSTER_SIZE environment variable in the pod specification was not updated from 3 to 5. This caused the newly created pods (docindex-3 and beyond) to fail their readiness probes.

**Evidence:** Pod docindex-3 logs show: "cluster: own ordinal 3 is outside the configured cluster (CLUSTER_SIZE=3); joining as standby, no shards assigned" and "http: listening on :8080 (/ready returns 503 while standby)". The pod status confirms docindex-3 is Running but not Ready, failing HTTP readiness probes with 503 status. Pod docindex-4 was never created because docindex-3 remained unready, blocking sequential pod creation.

**Fix:** Update the StatefulSet's pod template spec to set the CLUSTER_SIZE environment variable to 5 (or whatever the new desired replica count is). This can be done with: `kubectl patch statefulset docindex -n search -p '{\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"spec\":{\"containers\":[{\"name\":\"docindex\",\"env\":[{\"name\":\"CLUSTER_SIZE\",\"value\":\"5\"}]}]}}}}'` (adjust the environment variable section to match your pod's exact configuration). After updating, the existing pods will be rolled out and the new pods will join the cluster properly.
